scenario.description: An emergency department operations director must decide whether to open a temporary observation pod for the evening surge and finalize its capacity, staffing, monitoring, infection-control, and communication arrangements, with input from nursing, respiratory therapy, facilities, and language access.

shared_context.S1: The emergency department expects four additional observation patients between 18:00 and 22:00 today.
shared_context.S2: A temporary observation pod beside the emergency department is available for the evening if it is operationally ready.
shared_context.S3: Morgan makes the final decision about opening the pod and records its operating plan.
shared_context.S4: The pod has four stretchers, portable vital-sign monitors, and a wall oxygen supply; the operating plan records the pod's maximum permitted occupancy separately from the number of patients expected tonight.
shared_context.S5: At the 17:00 surge huddle, Morgan follows the routine readiness checklist by asking staffing, respiratory therapy, facilities, and language access for their exact operational requirements, then repeats each item back and records the responsible department before finalizing the plan.

PF1.text: For 18:00-22:00, the staffing roster provides exactly one float RN and one emergency-department technician for the pod; the evening staffing policy permits the pod to open for four observation patients with that one-RN/one-technician combination.

PF2.text: Patient C, one of the expected observation patients, has an order for continuous capnography because intermittent vital signs are not sufficient; portable capnography unit 2 is available and should be assigned to Patient C.

PF3.text: The fire-safety inspection sets the pod's maximum permitted occupancy at five patients, which is distinct from the four patients expected tonight. The handwashing station must be installed and tested before 17:30 for the pod to operate tonight.

PF4.text: Patient D, one of the expected observation patients, has requested an Arabic interpreter for the 19:00 reassessment; an Arabic interpreter is booked for 19:00-19:30.

acceptance_conditions: The temporary observation pod must open for the evening.
The recorded patient capacity must be five, as the fire-safety maximum rather than the four-patient expected census.
The pod must be staffed by exactly one RN and one emergency-department technician.
Continuous capnography must be assigned to Patient C.
The handwashing station readiness deadline must be recorded as 17:30.
A facilities commitment to install and test the handwashing station before 17:30 must be recorded.
The Arabic interpreter must be booked for Patient D from 19:00 to 19:30.
The facilities safety finding must be spoken aloud, credited, and cited in the final justification.
The respiratory-therapy finding must be formally revealed, credited, and cited in the final justification.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['facilities', 'handwashing_station', 'monitor_handwashing_station'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The staffing roster and evening policy change the required recorded coverage to exactly one float RN and one emergency-department technician for the four-patient pod.
Patient C's order and the available unit change the monitoring assignment to continuous capnography for Patient C and require the respiratory-therapy finding to be formally cited.

The fire-safety finding changes the recorded maximum capacity from the four-patient expected census to five, sets the readiness deadline to 17:30, and requires a facilities installation-and-testing commitment.
Patient D's language-access arrangement changes the communication plan to a confirmed Arabic interpreter from 19:00 to 19:30.
